/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 19 October 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2546 (35)
Baltic Capesize Index: 3365 (116)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2286 (-28)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1868 (3)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1016 (5)
CAPESIZE
The market made a positive start to the week, with improving sentiment across both the Pacific and Atlantic lifting the BCI 182 5TC by $1,054 to $30,518. The C5 index gained $0.745 to $12.445, while the C3 also advanced by $0.645 to $30.72. In the Pacific, following the resistance seen last Friday, C5 offers opened in the upper $12s to around $12.70. With two miners active alongside a handful of operators, there were unconfirmed reports of an operator fixing an earlier ETA at $12.50, while one miner was said to be bidding around $12.25 all before the index was published. The increased activity and firmer offers suggested owners were finding better support after last week’s decline. The Atlantic also showed signs of recovery, with the general consensus at the end of last week that the market had found a floor. Following reports of CSN fixing at $31 late on Friday, rumours circulated of a C3 fixture at $31.50 for mid-November loading, although details remained vague and the report was yet to be confirmed. For later dates, bids for end-November loading were said to be around $32.50. Overall, the market opened the week on a more encouraging note, with firmer sentiment across both basins and rates edging higher.
PANAMAX
Market participants described trading activity across both basins as having a typical Monday feel, with sentiment remaining under pressure, particularly in the Atlantic, resulting in the P5TC declining by $254 to $20,573. In the Atlantic, a wide bid-offer spread persists, with the limited bidding interest reportedly testing lower levels. Tonnage availability in the North Continent remains ample, although some sources noted the list is not as extensive as it was last week. Consequently, activity in both the trans-Atlantic and fronthaul markets was generally viewed as subdued. By contrast, the Pacific was described as largely flat, supported by a steady flow of demand from Australia and Indonesia. Some brokers suggested adverse weather conditions could have an impact on the market in the near term. However, charterers were reported to be testing rates below levels seen last week, and with fixture activity remaining limited, fresh market guidance was scarce. The Ionic Kibou (81,868 2015) open Surabaya 27 October was reported to have fixed for an Indonesia round trip at $23,750 plus $250,000 ballast bonus, although the charterer was not reported. K Line were reported to have covered their Dalrymple Bay stem to China and NYK also covered their East Coast Australia stem to Japan, but no other details were heard.
SUPRAMAX
As last week ended so quietly, it was no surprise that there were so few trades circulating today. The 11TC average was up slightly to $23,611, despite the US Gulf softening and posting the biggest movement, which had been muted last week as there was insufficient nearby demand. Elsewhere levels reflected a typically slow start to a new week. Sentiment in Asia remains positive and period has come to the fore as Charterers consider fixing below spot levels for longer duration trips, by locking in for longer with winter around the corner. Meanwhile, the ASP Frontier (57,298 2010) Bataan 21-24 October was fixed in the $26,000’s for trip via the Philippines to China intention nickel ore, but the Charterer was not reported.
HANDYSIZE
The Handysize market opened the week quietly, with sentiment largely driven by positional factors. The BHSI edged up by 5 points to 1,016, while the 7TC average rose by $80 to $18,280. The US Gulf remained flat and failed to gain momentum. Meanwhile, the South Atlantic maintained its upward trajectory, with participants remaining optimistic as rates strengthened further. Across the Continent and Mediterranean, conditions were mixed: more challenging trips achieved higher rates, while overall demand remained reasonably healthy. The Asian market also experienced a quiet start, with a relatively shorter tonnage list and enquiries continuing to be discussed at healthy levels.

Atlantic
The Tczew (39,072 2017) open Ravenna was fixed for a trip with delivery Canakkale and redelivery in the US Gulf carrying steel products at around $12,000, although further details were not disclosed.

Asia
A 34,000-dwt vessel open Malaysia was fixed for a trip with delivery on a dop basis via Australia to the Far East at $17,000. Separately, a 37,000-dwt vessel open Japan was fixed for a trip to the US West Coast with slag in the $17,000s, although further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
Chinese Steel Mill Activity

In the week to 16 October, Chinese blast furnace capacity utilisation eased 0.1 percentage point to 87.7%, while daily molten iron output held flat at 2.3 Mt/day, MySteel data show. The share of the 247 sampled mills in profit rose 1.3 percentage points on the week to 8.2%, but remains 47.2 percentage points below the same period last year. The blast furnace operation rate fell 0.9 percentage points to 80.5%, the lowest since March, whereas the EAF operation rate rose 1.2 percentage points to 72.6%, the highest since July.

Chinese Crude Steel Output

Chinese crude steel output lifted 0.1% year-on-year to 73.6 Mt in September, National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) data show. In the year-to-September, production stood at 724.8 Mt, 2.9% lower compared to the previous year.

[Sent from Front]

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape was sharply firmer overall, with heavy activity across Nov, Dec and Cal 27 as prices rallied throughout the morning and early afternoon. Oct strengthened from 32,250 to 33,150, while Nov opened at 34,000 before rallying to 35,500, easing towards 34,900 late. Dec opened at 36,000 before strengthening to 37,000, with the majority of volume around 36,500–36,750. Q4 26 improved from 34,000 to 35,000, while Q1 27 was paid up from 28,500 to 29,350 before easing to 29,000 late. Q2 27 traded around 34,500–34,800. Cal 27 strengthened from 31,900 to 32,400, with significant volume, including a 300-lot print at 32,400. Cal 28 traded at 27,500. Overall, Cape saw strong gains across the curve, particularly in Nov and Dec, despite some late profit-taking.
